correctness.rationale: PASS: The 3m listed cosmological vertices each have coordinate sum 1, and edge-vertex midpoints span the n+m standard basis affinely for graphs with no isolated vertices; affine dimension is d=n+m-1. With independent Gaussian coordinate vector the three scores for one edge have variance 3 and distinct covariance -1. For disjoint edges scores are independent; for incident edges, independent examination of the sign patterns gives exactly five +1 and four -1 cross-covariances, so absolute nontrivial correlations <=1/3 and the dependency neighborhood cardinality is O(N+Ω). With threshold a_N+b_N x and a_N,b_N calibrated to N(0,3), each event has probability O(1/N); the standard bivariate normal two-tail orthant inequality for abs correlation <=1/3 gives O(N^{-3/2}(log N)^{-1/4}) pair probability. Thus b1=O((N+Ω)/N²), b2=O((N+Ω)/[N^{3/2}(log N)^{1/4}]), b3=0, and the signed two-color rare-event process tends to independent Poisson counts; the upper and lower no-exceedance laws give independent Gumbel variables. Projection onto the sum-zero space subtracts a common scalar from every score and radial ||g_H||~sqrt d; the standardized radial error is O_P(log N/sqrt d)=o_P(1). For uniform degree bound D, a greedy matching of at least m/(2D-1) disjoint edges yields independent lower-tail witnesses for maxima, with union bounds for the upper tail, sufficient for uniform integrability of squares; a chi_d radius moment bound makes the normalized spherical error negligible in L². Therefore d Var W~π²/[2log(3m)] only for bounded degree. Verified covariance 5+/4- and exact projection identity independently for path m=4 and K5 m=10; these finite calculations do not prove the graph-sequence convergence. Dense graph Ω<=O(n^3)=O(m^{3/2}) is covered due to logarithm quarter; star Ω~m² excluded.
